components.title: Anatomy of coding agent workspaces and execution lifecycle
components.teaches: Students will understand the core architectural layers of an autonomous coding agent workspace, including environment virtualization, state tracking, and scratchpad management. They will trace how an agent transitions from prompt ingestion to planning, tool dispatch, and observation intake.

components.title: Context engineering strategies for constrained context windows
components.teaches: Students will learn context engineering mechanisms such as selective file tree pruning, sliding context windows, and dynamic relevance filtering. They will evaluate trade-offs between full repository indexing and lightweight context token budgets to prevent model distraction.

components.title: Structuring MCP tool schemas and workspace descriptors
components.teaches: Students will learn how to structure tool definitions using Model Context Protocol (MCP) JSON schemas so agents can discover and invoke workspace tools cleanly. They will specify required arguments, return payloads, and environment permissions according to MCP interface specifications.

components.title: Evaluating context pollution and tool discovery trade-offs
components.teaches: Students will analyse the failure modes caused by context pollution when exposing too many MCP tools or verbose tool definitions to a coding agent. They will compare lazy tool registration against global tool injection in terms of latency, token cost, and hallucinated invocations.

video.description:
Dexter Horthy, founder of Human Layer, shares what his team has learned about scaling coding agents in real-world software projects. He walks through why naive back-and-forth prompting fails, how spec-first development keeps teams aligned, and why “everything is context engineering.” From compaction strategies to subagents and planning workflows, he shows how intentional context management turns AI coding from prototypes into production.

00:09 - The Origin of Context Engineering
00:46 - Key Talks and Insights from AI Engineering
01:45 - Challenges with AI in Complex Systems
03:12 - The Shift to Spec-First Development
04:03 - Advanced Context Engineering for Coding Agents

video.description:
Agents need context (e.g., instructions, external knowledge, tool feedback) to perform tasks. Context engineering is the art and science of filling the context window with just the right information at each step of an agent’s trajectory. In this video, we break down some common strategies — write, select, compress, and isolate — for context engineering by reviewing various popular agents and papers. We then explain how LangGraph is designed to support them!

Blog:
https://blog.langchain.com/context-engineering-for-agents/

Video notes:
https://mirror-feeling-d80.notion.site/Context-Engineering-for-Agents-21f808527b17802db4b1c84a068a0976?source=copy_link
